children: Malaysia's 3Q GDP growth is expected to slow from the 6.0% growth in 2Q due to less favorable base effects and weaker mining production, economists at CIMB say. However, economists Chew Khai Yen and Michelle Chia estimate the growth to come in at 4.9%, higher than the 4.5% they projected earlier, driven by stronger palm oil production and electrical and electronics manufacturing. Slower trade volumes could suggest softer services growth, though improving employment and wage gains should continue to support private consumption, they say in a note. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
